name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.38.1 (released 2026-11-16, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.38.1) is a critical security release that hardens message templating against denial-of-service attacks including regex bombs, unbounded string/list construction, and self-referential template crashes. v2.38.0 added cluster-wide shared rate limiting across nodes and fixed a DoS bug in templating string amplification. Earlier v2.37.x releases improved UnifiedPush multi-server support, added Retry-After and RateLimit headers to rate-limited responses, and fixed a database performance regression.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL-2.0 (client) — dual-licensed; check repository for specifics
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in November 2026 with active bug fixes and security patches
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — user database, access control lists, rate limiting per user/IP, and subscriber-based rate limiting are supported
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud instance

breaking_excerpts: Message templating: printf no longer accepts explicit argument indexes or %p, and html/js/urlquery functions are disallowed — templates relying on these will break
UnifiedPush: a push to a topic with no subscriber for 4 days now returns 410 Gone (error 41002) instead of 507, causing app servers like Mastodon to remove the expired subscription
Message templating: regexMatch and related functions now reject patterns longer than 1024 bytes or compiling to more than 5000 instructions

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a powerful open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server with its own push infrastructure.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device push notifications with file sharing features but is a closed-source cloud service with a limited free tier and uncertain long-term development.

alternatives.name: ntopng / Bark
alternatives.review: Bark is a lightweight self-hosted iOS-focused push notification tool that is simpler than ntfy but limited to Apple devices and lacks Android or web support.
